items.title: Joseph "Fan" Bourgeau Interview, 1959-09-24
items.q: Piron played in the district many times

ctx.x: So you planned, not to cut your album out there, do you remember those bands that played in the dance halls in those days? In the district?

Well, Paul Dominguez played and I can't call this man's name. He played. Oh, I can't, he was a violin player. In them days lots of guys was playing violin. Can't call that gentleman's name to say my life. Piron was one. Piron played in the district many times and this fellow played and…
Did they have a big band this fellow you're thinking of? No, they didn't have a big band.

items.title: Joseph "Fan" Bourgeau Interview, 1972-09-13
items.q: P-Rone was a good violinist. He was a jazz violinist, you know what I mean?

ctx.x: I heard him on the records.

You heard him, man? Yeah. P-Rone was a good violinist. He was a jazz violinist, you know what I mean? Uh-huh. And he read music. He was first class. He used to play, he played out there on the lake for I don't know how long. Oh, I bought tranchinas? Tranchinas, that's right. That's why he played out. He had a six piece band. You know everybody in the band is dead? Uh-huh. Everybody in the band is dead.
